lines.text: Three whole-number sides that add up to twenty-four.
lines.caption: Three whole-number sides that add up to twenty-four.

lines.text: How many different triangles? Most kids miss one or two!
lines.caption: How many different triangles? Most kids miss one or two!

lines.text: How many different triangles have whole-number sides and a perimeter of twenty-four?
lines.caption: How many different triangles have whole-number sides and a perimeter of twenty-four?

lines.text: The same three sides count only once.
lines.caption: The same three sides count only once.

lines.text: Here's the trick. The longest side must be under twelve. That's half the perimeter.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. The longest side must be under twelve. That's half the perimeter.

lines.text: And at least eight, or the sides can't add up to twenty-four.
lines.caption: And at least eight, or the sides can't add up to twenty-four.

lines.text: So list the triangles by their longest side. Eleven, ten, nine, and eight.
lines.caption: So list the triangles by their longest side. Eleven, ten, nine, and eight.

lines.text: Five, plus four, plus two, plus one. That's twelve triangles, choice C!
lines.caption: Five, plus four, plus two, plus one. That's twelve triangles, choice C!

lines.text: Missing one or two is the classic slip. Listing by the longest side keeps you safe!
lines.caption: Missing one or two is the classic slip. Listing by the longest side keeps you safe!

lines.text: Why under half? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why under half? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
